key_insight: A video-language reasoning model (SOLE-R1) can serve as the sole reward function for on-robot reinforcement learning by evaluating egocentric video against language task descriptions, producing robust task success signals even under partial observability and distribution shift.
problem_solved: Current VLM-based evaluators are vulnerable to perceptual errors and distribution shift, allowing policies to exploit evaluator weaknesses rather than learning to solve tasks; SOLE-R1 addresses the need for a scalable, reliable reward source for real-world on-robot RL without human-in-the-loop labels.
method: Train/fine-tune a video-language reasoning model that ingests egocentric video sequences plus a language task prompt and predicts task success with temporal reasoning and uncertainty estimates.
Use the model as the sole reward generator in a closed-loop on-robot RL system: robot collects trajectories, SOLE-R1 scores them, and the policy is updated from that reward signal.
Mitigate reward hacking and distribution shift via temporal consistency checks, uncertainty-aware calibration, and continual on-robot data collection for periodic model adaptation.
impact: Enables scalable, autonomous robot learning from language-specified tasks without human labeling, improving robustness to perceptual errors and distribution shifts and making on-robot RL more practical for real-world deployment.

paper_title: SOLE-R1: Video-Language Reasoning as the Sole Reward for On-Robot Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Philip Schroeder, Thomas Weng, Karl Schmeckpeper, Eric Rosen, Stephen Hart
